doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Future plans, daughter, and closing
summary: Raph says he looks to the future, wants to stay active for his daughter, and the interview closes.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah, right. Good story. Glad I asked. In the future, you’re writing more stuff, you’re selective about your dates?

Writing a lot. Actually a large part of my life right now is my ten-year-old. I want to stay around long enough to give her a good shot at life. So the more years I can keep going and staying active in all of that, the better chance she has of relating and learning some
things that might be a little bit more difficult to learn otherwise. So that’s a big part of my life right now. I spend a lot of time with her, and we have a good relationship.

And what the future — it’s a funny thing to say the future, because I’m doing a lot of writing, and these trombone days that I have and the clinics and the Australian trip and all of that, these are in the future. I’ve always been a person looking in the future. I don’t look back. And I really have trouble — you know you’re asking me certain things that have happened, and I can remember them, but I don’t dwell on the past. I don’t think about well gee things used to be and wouldn’t it be nice if they still were and all of that. That’s absolutely ridiculous. So I’m always looking to the future. What am I going to have for lunch today. You know? What’s going to go on tomorrow, how’s next week’s particular thing going to go down.
Well it’s been fascinating talking with you.
It’s been fascinating being here. Thanks, Monk.
